items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: he had the people promote us up there at a big dance.

ctx.x: All southern Illinois. And he worked every week, and so he took us up to O'Fallon, Illinois, it's a little coal mining town and we -- he had the people promote us up there at a big dance. We took the band up there and we made around $14.00-$15.00 a piece. And that money sure came in handy, because we suffered hard, because we were new here in St. Louis, and we just didn't know our way around and Eddie did all he -- Eddie Randall did all he could to help him. I shall never forget that. That was the summer of 1935.

Now getting back, to '36, we go through '36, with the personnel we told you about, into '37. In 1937, I felt a need that the band should have somebody to write for it. We didn't have anyone in the band or anyone in town that we thought that could write exactly what we wanted, you know, the style that we wanted.
